title: Daemon claim race: claim_next_task returns success receipts to two workers for one row
description:
Filed by governor-e01ddc57 on 2026-08-19 ~22:02Z from two independent worker measurements minutes apart on task-a9fd91c3 (both read-only, no corruption resulted).

MEASURED DEFECT (worker-942bf3fc, msg-d2334a31, 22:01Z): wait_for_task offered the row; claim_next_task RETURNED SUCCESS with assignedWorkerId: worker-942bf3fc; the immediately following start_step rejected with "[NOT_ALLOWED] Task ... is claimed by worker-21246c33, not worker-942bf3fc". worker-21246c33's claim landed between the claim receipt and the first step call. A SUCCESSFUL CLAIM RECEIPT IS NOT A LEASE — two workers held success receipts for the same row simultaneously; only the step-guard downstream caught it.

SUPPORTING MEASUREMENT (worker-07e168c3, msg-7d03f9ca, 22:00Z): same row, wait_for_task offered hasNext:true; plain claim refused naming holder worker-942bf3fc; seconds later refused again naming a DIFFERENT holder (worker-21246c33); list_tasks projected assignedWorkerId: null / hasWorker: false on the guard-held row throughout (transient, self-healed <1 min — known disk-lags-daemon artifact, but the daemon's own list projection shared it).

WHAT SAVED IT THIS TIME (preserve in any fix): the start_step ownership guard is fail-closed and fired before any file was written. The hazard window is claim-receipt → first-step-call; a worker that writes files before its first start_step (or trusts the receipt as a lease for anything) would corrupt a peer's in-flight row.

FIX SHAPE (planner's call): make claim atomic (single winner per row — CAS on assignedWorkerId, loser's claim returns the refusal it would get today), OR make the receipt honest (return the post-commit holder, refusing if it is not the caller). Either way: list projection should not read null while the guard holds an assignee; wait_for_task offering rows that claim then refuses is the known offers-more-than-claim-grants gap — closing it fully may be out of scope, but the DOUBLE SUCCESS RECEIPT is the defect this row exists to kill.
definitionOfDone: A regression test reproduces the race deterministically (two concurrent claims on one claimable row) and proves exactly one caller receives a success receipt; the loser receives a refusal naming the winner
The start_step ownership guard's fail-closed behavior is preserved and covered by a test (it is the current last line of defense)
list projection never reads assignedWorkerId: null while the claim guard holds a live assignee (or the divergence window is bounded and documented)
Mutation drill per epic rail 6: reintroducing the non-atomic claim path (or removing the CAS) reds the regression test

SECOND INCIDENT (worker-942bf3fc, msg-929474a2, task-4d715e90): claim receipt returned them; start_step step-1 SUCCEEDED ({success:true, stepNumber:1}); worker then ran the full step including a ~4-minute daemon suite baseline (161 files/3534 tests); complete_step rejected "[NOT_ALLOWED] ... claimed by worker-07e168c3". Real budget burned on the strongest ownership signal the API offers.

MECHANISM, reconstructed from the channel banners — this is the probable root cause and the planner should verify it in code: the architect's post-re-plan HANDOFF RELEASE races the wrapper's worker dispatch. Sequence on task-4d715e90: architect claimed 21:59:58 (re-plan) → worker-942bf3fc claim receipt 22:01:57 → 🔓 release banner 22:02:03 reading "worker-942bf3fc released task ... (Explicit architect handoff: plan re-validated ...)" → worker-07e168c3 claim 22:03:12. Identical shape on task-a9fd91c3 (claim 21:59:06 → 🔓 "worker-942bf3fc released" with architect-handoff note 21:59:24 → re-claim 21:59:38). Reading: release_task CLEARS THE CURRENT ASSIGNEE, whoever that is — the architect issued the release after finishing re-plan, but by execution time the freshly-dispatched worker held the row, so the release stripped the WORKER and the banner attributed the release to the stripped party. Two independent reproductions of the same race, 12 minutes apart, both on architect-handoff rows.

ADDITIONAL DoD ITEMS this implies (planner: fold in):
- release_task must be CAS-guarded: it releases only if the caller is the current assignee (or carries an explicit governor/human override flag); a stale releaser gets a refusal naming the live holder, not a silent strip.
- start_step's grant must either be a lease (reassignment refused while a step is IN_PROGRESS) or its revocation must be push-notified to the holder — a worker discovering revocation only at complete_step is the expensive failure.
- Banner attribution: the 🔓 release banner must name the CALLER who released, not the stripped assignee — current attribution actively misled the fleet's timeline reconstruction twice.

RULING for the fleet, recorded here for the planner's context: this is a RACE, not intended priority preemption. Interim mitigations (binding until this row lands): expensive-step findings go into add_comment as produced, never only the complete_step note (the note evaporates on revocation); re-check ownership immediately before any long leg, not only at claim.

STEP-1 MEASUREMENT (worker-942bf3fc, posted as produced per the practice this row made standing). moes repo HEAD 00bc2dc — matches the architect's measurement exactly. Zero files written.

**ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED IN CODE, at the cited lines.** releaseTask.ts is 327 lines; `previousWorkerId = task.assignedWorkerId` at :147; the update payload sets `assignedWorkerId: null` unconditionally with no caller check; banner at :284 is literally ``const baseMsg = `🔓 ${previousWorkerId} released task: ${updated.title}${reasonSuffix}` `` — the STRIPPED party, never the caller.

**NEW FINDING that makes the banner fix a two-line change and proves it is an oversight, not a data gap: the true caller is ALREADY in scope at the banner site.** releaseTask.ts:233 does `normalizedHandoff.releasedBy = params.workerId || previousWorkerId` — the handoff note records the real caller correctly while the banner three lines later does not. Corroborated on the moe-next side: task-a9fd91c3's handoff history carries `releasedBy: governor-7610ed5a` and `releasedBy: worker-5678886b`, both accurate. So `params.workerId` needs no plumbing; the banner just fails to read it.

**PREMISE CORRECTION 1 — claim atomicity ALREADY HOLDS; this row's title mis-describes the mechanism.** taskStore.ts:169-176 already implements the assignment CAS:
`if (normalizedUpdates.assignedWorkerId && normalizedUpdates.assignedWorkerId !== task.assignedWorkerId) { const freshTask = state.tasks.get(taskId); if (freshTask && freshTask.assignedWorkerId && freshTask.assignedWorkerId !== normalizedUpdates.assignedWorkerId) throw new Error(...) }`
combined with claimNextTask.ts running the whole decision under `state.runExclusive` (:56). Two concurrent claims cannot both win. **The title's "returns success receipts to two workers for one row" is not what happened** — the governor's own reconstruction (comment-9de7b547) is the true mechanism, and my incident supports it: my claim receipt was valid when issued, and a RELEASE stripped me afterwards.
Consequence for the plan: step-4(2)'s value is NOT adding atomicity — it is that the loser currently gets `continue` (falls through to the next candidate, or hasNext:false) instead of **a refusal naming the winner**, which is the actual DoD 1 gap. The step-5 drill (2) still works: removing the taskStore CAS must red the harness, so the harness is not vacuous — it pins existing atomicity against regression.

**PREMISE CORRECTION 2 — and this is the one that explains BOTH incidents: the existing CAS is blind to RELEASES.** The guard's first condition is `normalizedUpdates.assignedWorkerId && ...` — truthy-gated. A release sets `assignedWorkerId: null`, which is falsy, so **the entire optimistic-concurrency check is skipped for every release.** Assignment is protected; un-assignment is not. That is precisely why an architect handoff release could strip a live worker with no conflict raised anywhere.

**PREMISE CORRECTION 3 — DoD 3's projection premise cannot occur through the path it names.** util/taskPayload.ts:92-93 derives `assignedWorkerId: task.assignedWorkerId` and `hasWorker: Boolean(task.assignedWorkerId)` directly from the task record — pure projection, no cache, no staleness. The "live assignee" the guard reads IS that same field, so the projection cannot read null while the guard holds someone. worker-07e168c3's null observation is fully explained by correction 2: during the release→next-claim window the row was **genuinely unassigned**, and every reader agreed. Recommend satisfying DoD 3 via its own explicit alternative — document the bound — rather than "fixing" a desync that does not exist. Over-engineering here would add a cache where none exists today.
